notes.subject: car
notes.text: The coverage car is usually black and white, and the camera sits very low: big blur at the bottom and a wide-looking road.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Traffic drives on the left side of the road.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Mix of kanji and two softer syllabic scripts; the rounded, looping one is hiragana, the angular one katakana, common in ads.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Round concrete utility poles with screw-like steps up the side, loaded with plates, guy wires and transformers.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Short pole reflector pads that stay off the ground, usually yellow or white stripes, vertical or diagonal.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Short white plates with green text; light cars (kei) get short yellow plates with black text.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: White solid edge lines with a dashed white or solid yellow centre line; yellow is never used on the edge.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Plain white bollard with a round reflector on top; some are black or carry a place name in kanji.

notes.subject: guardrail
notes.text: Simple plain white guardrails are the default.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Prefectural roads use hexagonal shields, with the road number and often the prefecture written below in kanji.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: The stop sign is a distinctive downward-pointing triangle with local text.

notes.subject: street
notes.text: Curved traffic mirrors at junctions, school crossing signs and heavy retaining walls on rural slopes are all common.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Very mountainous and forested, with small flat areas such as the Kanto and Nobi plains, plus dense rice paddies.

notes.subject: street
notes.text: Vertical traffic lights occur in the far north island and along the northwest coast; horizontal ones elsewhere.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Phone area codes get higher as you go south; codes ending in 0, like 0120, are not regional.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Each electric-company region has its own style of pole plate, so plates help narrow the area.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Plus-shaped side bar or a single transformer on two bars; never a wooden plate.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Arrows marking the road edge under snow are found almost only on the northern island.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Kerosene and gas tanks are more common further north and in high mountains, and are abundant on the northern island.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Giant butterbur leaves, called cabbage, grow along roadsides in the north and are much smaller further south.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Cyrillic text appears on signs in a couple of far northern towns near Russia.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Thick white bollard with an octagonal reflector and a yellow stripe below it.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Same thick octagonal-reflector bollard but with two yellow stripes underneath.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Extendable white bollard with a round reflector and two yellow stripes.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Extendable single-reflector bollard with a red stripe under the reflector.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Octagonal reflector and red stripe, with a sloped join where base meets top.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Flat white bollard with separated orange reflectors on one face only.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Some bollards carry a black stripe just under the reflector.

notes.subject: guardrail
notes.text: Green bands on guardrails, most common in Oita and Miyazaki.

notes.subject: guardrail
notes.text: Distinctive yellow guardrails.

notes.subject: guardrail
notes.text: Red and yellow striped stickers on guardrail ends across this region, except Yamaguchi.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Orange and black bands wrapped around utility poles.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Black signs with two yellow circles.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Cycle routes marked with a white outer line and blue inner line.

notes.subject: street
notes.text: Tiny circular nozzles in the pavement spray warm water to melt snow, mainly on northwest coastal roads.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Distinctive red-tiled roofs, especially in Hiroshima and Shimane.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Roofs turn flat or low-sloped further north and in snowy mountains, often with ladders up the side.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: White concrete buildings with flat roofs, often with guardian lion statues.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: Sugarcane fields appear almost only on the southern Kyushu islands and Okinawa; red soil fields on the far southern islands.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: Hedged rows of tea with frost-fans on poles, mostly around Shizuoka and Kagoshima.
